top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: The United States put 50 per cent tariffs on about US$20 billion of Canadian goods just after midnight, and Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended negotiations and promised to retaliate dollar for dollar. That rupture set the tone for a day of hard edges: Washington publishes its promised 'toughest sanctions in history' on Iran on Monday, with oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz already close to a standstill. In Ukraine, rescuers spent the night pulling people from a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre hit twice by Russian drones, a toll now at 16 dead and 130 injured. Most of the rest of the day belonged to courts and regulators rather than politicians — a US judge struck down a visa ban covering applicants from 75 countries, with a run of other rulings and settlements behind it. Monday is the day to watch: the Iran package and a Franco-British-German meeting on Ukraine land within hours of each other.

stories.headline: US imposes 50% tariffs on Canadian goods after trade talks collapse
stories.summary: Washington put 50 per cent tariffs on roughly US$20 billion (C$28 billion) of Canadian goods just after midnight US time on Aug 22 — noon in Singapore — after days of talks broke down minutes before the deadline. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he had suspended negotiations and recalled his negotiators, calling late US changes to the terms “unfair, uneconomic”, and said Canada would retaliate dollar for dollar. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Canada had declined to finalise a deal agreed earlier in the week. The affected goods are just over 5 per cent of Canada’s exports to the US, but the rupture complicates the coming renegotiation of the US-Mexico-Canada trade pact.

stories.headline: TikTok to pay US$400 million to settle US children’s privacy case
stories.summary: TikTok and parent ByteDance agreed to pay US$400 million (about S$500 million) to end a US Justice Department lawsuit alleging they collected data on millions of users under 13 without parental consent, in breach of the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act. The 2024 case is being dismissed with prejudice. It is one of the largest COPPA settlements to date — Google’s YouTube paid US$170 million in 2019 and Epic Games US$275 million in 2022. Meta is separately on trial over similar claims brought by attorneys-general in 29 states.

stories.headline: Rescuers search Kryvyi Rih mall rubble after double-tap strike kills 16
stories.summary: Ukrainian rescuers worked through the night in the wreckage of a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre struck twice by Russian drones on Friday. Regional military head Oleksandr Hanzha said the toll reached 16 dead and 130 injured, including 23 children, after another body was recovered overnight; nine people are reported still missing. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the second wave targeted emergency workers at the scene, footage the BBC says it verified. Russia’s defence ministry said it had targeted transport infrastructure and warehouses and has not commented on the mall. Local officials said at least two more people were killed in further Russian strikes early on Saturday.

stories.headline: US and Iran trade defiant messages ahead of Monday’s sanctions announcement
stories.summary: With the war approaching six months, the two sides are neither exchanging fire nor talking. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will detail what he has promised will be “the toughest sanctions in history” at a press conference on Monday and is pressing Beijing — which buys more than 80 per cent of Iran’s shipped oil, on 2025 Kpler data — to cooperate. Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called the measures an “assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty” with no basis in international law. Oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has all but stopped: ship-tracking data showed only four commodity ships transited on Thursday, none of them crude or LNG carriers.

stories.headline: Australia’s capital territory joins gun buyback after Bondi Beach attack
stories.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the Australian Capital Territory has agreed to join the national gun buyback, following New South Wales, which was first to commit and will launch its scheme on Nov 2. The buyback, tighter licence checks and a crackdown on hate speech were legislated in January after the Dec 14 shooting at a Hanukkah celebration at Bondi Beach in Sydney that killed 15 people. Albanese said the aim was to ensure “an antisemitic terrorist attack like we saw at Bondi can’t happen again”.

stories.headline: Turkey to seek Interpol red notice for Netanyahu over Gaza flotilla case
stories.summary: Turkey said on Aug 21 it would ask Interpol for a red notice to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as part of a domestic criminal case over Israel’s interception of activists trying to deliver aid to Gaza. Ankara accuses Israel of genocide and crimes against humanity; Israel rejects the charges and called the move a “pathetic attempt” to intimidate its leaders and soldiers. Netanyahu responded by calling President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an “antisemitic dictator”. Relations between the two NATO-adjacent powers have deteriorated over Gaza and over rival influence in Syria.

stories.headline: Netherlands fines Uber €825 million over automated driver deactivations
stories.summary: The Dutch data protection authority confirmed a €825 million (about S$1.2 billion) fine against Uber for deactivating drivers’ accounts without telling them, in breach of European rules barring decisions based solely on automated processing. The judgement was agreed on Aug 17 and relates to incidents in Europe between 2020 and 2022. The complaint originated in France but was heard in the Netherlands because Uber’s European headquarters are in Amsterdam. Uber called the penalty “disproportionate” and said it will appeal.

stories.headline: US judge strikes down visa suspension covering applicants from 75 countries
stories.summary: US District Judge Jeannette Vargas in Manhattan ruled on Aug 21 that a State Department policy suspending immigrant visas for applicants from 75 countries was “patently unlawful” and exceeded Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s statutory authority. The policy, announced and effective from January, covered applicants from Latin America, the Balkans, South Asia and much of Africa, the Middle East and the Caribbean, on the grounds they were at high risk of becoming a public charge. The judge said federal law explicitly removed the secretary of state’s authority over consular officers’ processing of immigrant visas.

stories.headline: Pentagon fires Stars and Stripes editor-in-chief and publisher
stories.summary: Leadership at Stars and Stripes, which has covered the US military since the Civil War, told US media on Aug 21 that the Pentagon had dismissed editor-in-chief Erik Slavin and publisher Max Lederer. Slavin told CBS News he was fired for “insubordination” after an interview in which he described disagreements with the Department of Defence; Lederer had announced his retirement three days earlier. Reporter Lara Korte said she was also sacked. The department said earlier this year it wanted to steer the paper’s coverage away from “woke distractions”. The publication is partly DOD-funded but has long maintained editorial independence.

stories.headline: Boeing engineers reject contract and authorise a strike
stories.summary: The 17,000 members of SPEEA, Boeing’s largest white-collar union, voted down a four-year contract offer on Aug 21 — engineers 64 per cent against, technical workers about 72 per cent — and gave their negotiating team the power to call a strike once the current contract expires on Oct 6. Members objected to wage increases capped at 3 per cent against Seattle-area inflation of 4.5 per cent. No new talks are scheduled. Boeing said it would activate a strike contingency plan to protect production.

stories.headline: One killed in sword attack at Swedish high school
stories.summary: Police were called to the Brinell School in Fagersta, central Sweden, shortly after 2pm local time on Friday, where officers fired at and then arrested an 18-year-old man. One person was killed, two teenage boys were seriously injured and another suffered minor injuries. Eight nearby schools were locked down and a state of high alert was declared in the Västmanland region; both have since been lifted. Local media reported the suspect was a former student. Police said they were still working to establish a motive and saw no continuing danger to the public.

stories.headline: US health department opens public comment on federal vaccine recommendations
stories.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services said on Aug 21 it was seeking public feedback on how federal vaccine recommendations are categorised and communicated, following President Donald Trump’s executive order calling for fewer childhood vaccinations. The notice asks whether some vaccines should be recommended but not in infancy, or recommended with qualifications, and how timing and sequencing should be handled — including wider age windows or separate visits. Parents, doctors and health officials have until Sep 20 to comment.

stories.headline: China and Indonesia agree to deepen military ties and cooperation on minerals and tech
stories.summary: Beijing and Jakarta agreed to expand defence cooperation and work more closely on critical minerals, energy and technology, deepening a relationship that already makes China Indonesia’s largest trading partner and a major investor in its nickel industry. The agreement lands as South-east Asian governments weigh their positions between Washington and Beijing amid the Iran conflict and the widening US tariff campaign.

stories.headline: CNA Explains: why Trump is pushing to meet Kim Jong Un again
stories.summary: CNA sets out why the US president is again seeking a summit with North Korea’s leader, and what has changed since their first-term meetings — including the scaling of US-South Korea military exercises and Pyongyang’s deepened alignment with Moscow. The explainer comes days after North Korea launched 10 ballistic missiles as the latest allied drills wound down.

stories.headline: Migrants who refused deportation to Liberia sent to Equatorial Guinea
stories.summary: Migrants who resisted removal to Liberia under a US deportation arrangement were instead flown to Equatorial Guinea, sources told The Straits Times’ wire partners. The account has not been confirmed on the record by US or host-government officials. The transfers are part of the Trump administration’s push to place deportees in third countries that agree to receive them.

stories.headline: US starts transfer of US$725 million towards its UN arrears
stories.summary: A congressional notification seen by wire reporters shows the Trump administration has begun the process of transferring US$725 million (about S$920 million) to the United Nations, against more than US$4 billion in dues the US owes. Washington did not immediately respond to questions. The UN secretary-general has warned of a financial squeeze as arrears mount, and a member state that falls too far behind risks losing its General Assembly vote. Several other members, including China, have also delayed payments this year.

stories.headline: Earthquake damages buildings and cuts power in Peru
stories.summary: A strong earthquake damaged buildings and caused power cuts in Peru, the BBC reported on Aug 21. Assessments of casualties and structural damage were still under way at the time of reporting, and no official toll had been published.

stories.headline: Lula holds lead over Flavio Bolsonaro in latest Brazil election poll
stories.summary: A Datafolha survey shows President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva still ahead of challenger Flavio Bolsonaro as Brazil’s election approaches. Separately, Brazil’s government said Trump told Lula in a phone call that officials from the two sides should meet soon to discuss tariffs.

stories.headline: Former Guyana minister leads second straw poll for UN secretary-general
stories.summary: A former Guyanese minister came out on top in the Security Council’s second informal straw poll to choose the next UN secretary-general. Straw polls are non-binding soundings of council members’ preferences and can shift substantially between rounds; the council must eventually recommend a single candidate to the General Assembly.

stories.headline: At least 13 Tunisians missing after migrant boat sinks
stories.summary: A migrant rights group said at least 13 Tunisians are missing after their boat sank off Tunisia. The figure comes from the group rather than an official rescue authority and has not been independently confirmed. It follows the burial in Spain’s Ceuta enclave of the first victims of a deadly border rush earlier in the week.

stories.headline: Airbus drops return-to-office mandate after staff protests
stories.summary: Airbus has backed away from a plan to require more days in the office after protests from employees, sources told wire reporters. The company has not confirmed the reversal publicly. It is one of the larger European employers to retreat from a tightened office-attendance policy, a pattern that has played out unevenly across the aerospace and tech sectors.

stories.headline: UK court orders Prince Harry and six others to pay Daily Mail publisher £9.5 million
stories.summary: A UK court ordered Prince Harry, Elton John and five other claimants to pay £9.5 million in costs to Associated Newspapers, publisher of the Daily Mail, after their unlawful information-gathering case against the group failed. The claimants had alleged phone-tapping and other intrusive practices, which the publisher denied.

stories.headline: India’s Vantara zoo announces a ‘reset’ and rethinks animal imports
stories.summary: Vantara, the vast private animal facility built by an Indian tycoon’s family, said it would “reset” its operations and reconsider its programme of importing animals from abroad. The centre has drawn scrutiny over the scale and sourcing of its collection; the announcement signals a narrower future intake.

stories.headline: UK forecasters say the coming El Nino could be the biggest on record
stories.summary: Britain’s Met Office forecasts that the developing El Nino will be the strongest measured and is likely to push global temperatures to a new annual record. El Nino events warm the tropical Pacific and shift rainfall patterns worldwide; for South-east Asia they typically mean hotter, drier conditions and a higher risk of haze — a pattern already visible in this month’s Borneo fires.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: SimplyGo has fixed the configuration error that stripped morning pre-peak discounts from an average of 210,000 journeys a day on Aug 20 and 21, and says corrected fares now show in the app. Two changes with longer reach also landed: service fees for HDB's assisted-living flats will be cut by 18 to 75 per cent from 2027, and LTA wants authorised exporters rather than owners held responsible for deregistered cars after illegal road use nearly doubled. Sunday's National Day Rally is expected to lead on marriage and parenthood, and the courts had a heavy day of their own. The talk is scam-and-kindness flavoured — AI clones of local influencers selling cosmetics on TikTok on one side, secondary school students tracking down a wallet's owner through his NRIC on the other. If you drive, note the Ang Mo Kio closures on Sunday; if you tap in before 7.45am, check your Aug 20 and 21 fares.

stories.headline: SimplyGo fixes pre-peak discount glitch that hit 210,000 journeys a day
stories.summary: A configuration error stopped morning pre-peak discounts being applied to SimplyGo EZ-Link and bank-card taps on Aug 20 and 21, affecting an average of 210,000 journeys a day. SimplyGo said in a Facebook post on Aug 21 that the issue has been rectified and that correct fares — with discounts where eligible — now show in the app and are what will be charged. Commuters who tapped in before the 7.45am cut-off had complained on social media of being charged full fares. The scheme, running since 2017, gives up to 50 cents off weekday rail trips started before 7.45am.

stories.headline: LTA proposes shifting responsibility for deregistered cars to authorised exporters
stories.summary: Under a proposed Authorised Exporter Scheme, owners who hand a deregistered car to an authorised party would no longer carry the obligation to prove it was properly disposed of — the authorised exporter would. LTA is also considering paying out residual COE and PARF rebates immediately on handover, instead of the four to seven days dealers say they currently wait. The proposal follows a rise in deregistered vehicles being driven illegally: 122 cases in the first five months of 2026, close to double the whole of 2024. Public feedback closes on Aug 28, with a transition period of at least a year for the trade.

stories.headline: Community care apartment service fees to be cut by 18% to 75% from 2027
stories.summary: Monthly basic service package fees for HDB’s assisted-living flats will fall by between 18 and 75 per cent from 2027, and the eligibility age drops from 65 to 55, after rising service costs dampened demand. Of the five projects launched so far — in Bukit Batok, Queenstown, Bedok, Geylang and Sengkang — only the first two were oversubscribed; Sengkang drew an application rate of 0.7. The flats, a joint MOH, MND and HDB offering, pair senior-friendly design with care and social services.

stories.headline: Marriage and parenthood expected to lead PM Wong’s National Day Rally on Aug 23
stories.summary: Analysts expect family formation to feature heavily in Sunday’s Rally, framed less as a call to have more children than as making family life compatible with people’s wider aspirations, given Singapore’s very low fertility rate. In his National Day Message, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said a major review was under way of how families are supported across life stages, and that more detail on help with the costs of raising children would come in the Rally speech.

stories.headline: Road and lane closures in Ang Mo Kio for the National Day Rally on Aug 23
stories.summary: Police said several roads and lanes near ITE College Central will be shut to vehicles from 5am to 11.59pm on Aug 23, including Ang Mo Kio Drive, both slip roads linking it to Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5, and the extreme left lane of Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5. Only authorised and emergency vehicles will be allowed through, parking restrictions will be enforced and illegally parked vehicles may be towed. PM Wong’s Rally speech begins at 6.45pm.

stories.headline: DBS and POSB digital payment services restored after late-night disruption
stories.summary: DBS said on Facebook at about 11.20pm on Aug 21 that customers using FAST, PayNow and SGQR on digibank and PayLah may be affected, and posted just before midnight that services were back to normal as of 11.34pm. Downdetector logged a spike in reports from about 10.15pm. The bank advised card payments and ATM withdrawals in the interim and said deposits remained safe. It follows a PayLah outage on Jul 23 and a roughly hour-long digital banking disruption in March.

stories.headline: Four fatal HDB fires in 19 days expose the difficulty of evacuating frail seniors
stories.summary: Four fatal fires in HDB estates between Jul 28 and Aug 16 killed residents aged between 65 and 88, and MPs and social service agencies say the evacuation of older residents with mobility problems is the weak link. The point was underlined again by an Aug 20 blaze at Block 979B Buangkok Crescent, where about 220 people were evacuated and neighbours had to help an 83-year-old woman with a walker down to the ground floor. Agencies are looking at emergency alert systems, clearer evacuation plans and targeted fire-safety education for vulnerable seniors.

stories.headline: Woman motorcyclist, 45, dies after two-bike accident on the BKE
stories.summary: Police were alerted at about 11.30am on Aug 21 to an accident involving two motorcycles on the BKE towards the PIE. A 32-year-old man was taken to hospital conscious; a 45-year-old woman was taken unconscious and later died. SCDF took one person to Tan Tock Seng Hospital and another to Woodlands Hospital. Motorcyclists and pillion riders made up 54.8 per cent of all traffic accidents and 53 per cent of deaths in 2025 despite motorcycles being about 15 per cent of the vehicle population, with cases rising from 3,973 in 2024 to 4,227 in 2025.

stories.headline: Tree falls on two cars in Dempsey; spa staff free trapped driver
stories.summary: A private-hire driver, 60, was turning out of the Museum of Ice Cream along Loewen Road on Aug 22 when a tree toppled onto the passenger side of his MPV, crushing the roof and trapping him inside. Staff from a nearby spa freed him before SCDF and an ambulance arrived; he was checked and found uninjured, and SCDF said no ambulance assistance was needed. A parked BMW was also damaged. Loewen Road remained blocked as of 12.45pm while contractors cleared the tree.

stories.headline: Car fire in Toa Payoh carpark draws a crowd of onlookers, many of them children
stories.summary: SCDF was alerted at about 6pm on Aug 21 to a car fire at an open-air carpark at Block 148 Lorong 1 Toa Payoh. The blaze involved the engine compartment and was put out with a water jet, with no reported injuries; the cause is under investigation. Video posted on TikTok showed sparks and thick smoke, and a crowd standing close by that included children in school uniform.

stories.headline: Aunt of convicted child abuser charged with failing to protect children in her care
stories.summary: A 46-year-old woman who ran a private educational facility faces two charges under the Children and Young Persons Act for allegedly knowingly permitting her nephew to continue caring for children she knew he was abusing. She cannot be named because it would identify victims protected by a gag order. Her nephew, a 31-year-old Singaporean, was sentenced on Aug 21 to nine years and 10 months’ jail and eight strokes of the cane. The charge sheets are dated April 2024; she faces up to eight years’ jail and a fine.

stories.headline: Man jailed nine years, 10 months and caned for abusing a six-year-old for 18 hours
stories.summary: A 31-year-old Singaporean was sentenced on Aug 21 to nine years and 10 months’ jail and eight strokes of the cane after pleading guilty to abusing primary school pupils at a private educational facility, including forcing a six-year-old boy to hold a push-up position for 18 hours and to drink his own urine. The victims are protected by a gag order.

stories.headline: Pandan Reservoir crocodile photo was fake, PUB files police report
stories.summary: PUB said the photograph that triggered a search and the suspension of water activities at Pandan Reservoir was found to be fake, and it has lodged a police report. Water activities had been halted and a search-and-capture operation launched after the image circulated on Aug 20. Police are investigating.

stories.headline: Police block website that falsely claimed links to the Foreign Affairs Ministry
stories.summary: Singapore police have blocked access to a website that falsely claimed affiliation with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Sites impersonating government agencies are commonly used to lend credibility to investment and advance-fee scams; the authorities urge the public to verify official links through gov.sg domains.

stories.headline: Government begins beta testing a chatbot for official information
stories.summary: The Singapore government is beta testing a chatbot intended to make official information easier to find, letting users ask questions in plain language instead of navigating individual agency sites. It is a trial rather than a full launch, and the government has said such tools sit alongside, not in place of, official agency channels.

stories.headline: Two Traffic Police officers hospitalised after their vehicle caught fire on the BKE
stories.summary: Two Traffic Police officers were taken to hospital for smoke inhalation after their vehicle caught fire on the BKE on Aug 21. It was the second vehicle incident reported on the expressway that day.

stories.headline: TikTok ads use AI clones of influencer Dewy Choo and actor Zhang Linghe to target Singaporeans
stories.summary: Influencer Dewy Choo, 24, told The Straits Times she found an ad on TikTok in July using her likeness and voice without consent to sell false eyelashes. Ads from the same anonymous account used AI-generated images of Chinese actor Zhang Linghe at East Coast Park and Marina Bay to sell mascara and caps. Choo, who has nearly half a million followers, said the fake’s face matched hers down to the eyebrows and jaw. The case adds to a run of AI-impersonation scams aimed at Singapore users.

stories.headline: Woman charged over $32 million luxury goods ruse as Tradeluxury director faces money-laundering charge
stories.summary: A woman was charged with allegedly handling $35,000 of proceeds from a $32 million luxury goods scheme in which customers paid upfront for handbags and other goods. Separately, a director of Tradeluxury was charged with money laundering in the same case. The charges are allegations that have yet to be tested in court.

stories.headline: MOM investigating claim that an airport wheelchair assistant had $5 docked for being 11 seconds late
stories.summary: The Ministry of Manpower said it is looking into claims that an airport wheelchair assistant had S$5 deducted from pay for clocking in 11 seconds late. The Employment Act permits deductions for absence from work but requires them to be proportionate to the time not worked. The companies named in the account have not publicly commented on the specifics.

stories.headline: Singapore and Vietnam to hold their first strategic dialogue on Aug 25
stories.summary: The two countries will hold an inaugural strategic dialogue on Aug 25, a standing channel for senior officials to coordinate on security, economic and regional issues. Singapore and Vietnam upgraded ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2025, and Vietnam is one of Singapore’s larger investment destinations in South-east Asia.

stories.headline: 3,000 lower-income residents in the north-east to get $500 each in warm meal credits
stories.summary: Warm Meals @ North East, launched by OCBC and the North East CDC on Aug 21 at Block 603A Tampines Avenue 9, will give 1,000 households in Tampines, Punggol and Pasir Ris-Changi $500 in meal credits each — about 165 meals, redeemable at roughly 30 food lockers at or near the void decks of HDB rental blocks. The programme aims to provide 165,000 meals to more than 3,000 residents over a year from September.

stories.headline: 81 arrested in four-day islandwide drug operation; weapons found in Punggol flat
stories.summary: The Central Narcotics Bureau arrested 81 suspected drug offenders in a four-day islandwide operation and seized drugs worth more than S$105,000. Officers also recovered katanas and knuckledusters from a Punggol flat during the sweep.

stories.headline: LTA to use AI on bus cameras to spot bus-lane offences and road defects
stories.summary: LTA will roll out an AI system that reads footage from cameras already fitted to public buses to detect motorists driving in bus lanes and to flag road defects for repair. Using the bus fleet as a moving sensor network extends enforcement and inspection coverage without new roadside hardware.

stories.headline: YouTube Premium raises prices in Singapore across subscription plans
stories.summary: Google is raising YouTube Premium prices in Singapore across its individual, family and student plans. Existing subscribers are typically given notice before the new rate applies at their next billing cycle.

stories.headline: Apple impersonation scams cost Singapore victims at least $195,000 in crypto in two weeks
stories.summary: Police said on Aug 21 that at least five cases have been reported since Aug 7 with losses totalling at least $195,000 in cryptocurrency. Victims get a pop-up on an Apple device claiming unauthorised access to their account, then an unsolicited call from someone posing as Apple technical support who walks them through fake sites to harvest Apple ID credentials, crypto account details and one-time passwords. Police stress Apple never asks for credentials by call or pop-up, and urge users to check account status through official channels and report calls to the ScamShield Helpline.

stories.headline: CNA analysis shows how scammers spliced real footage of PM Wong into a fake Zoom call
stories.summary: CNA published an analysis of a scam the Singapore Police Force disclosed in May, in which a victim transferred at least S$4.9 million after being placed in a fake Zoom conference. SPF shared the full recording with CNA. The call was assembled largely from real but out-of-context footage — including a April 2022 government press conference by then-Finance Minister Lawrence Wong — to make it appear that Singaporean and global leaders were seeking help to stabilise trade through the Strait of Hormuz. Footage of President Tharman Shanmugaratnam and Minister Indranee Rajah was also used.

stories.headline: Police appeal for information on missing 13-year-old girl last seen in Jurong West
stories.summary: Police are appealing for information on a 13-year-old girl last seen near Westwood Avenue in Jurong West on Aug 19. Anyone with information is asked to call the police hotline or submit it online.

stories.headline: HSA halts sales and recalls Medicube cream suspected of containing a banned dye
stories.summary: The Health Sciences Authority told Mothership it has worked with the three companies marketing Medicube PDRN Pink Collagen Capsule Cream to suspend sales and recall the product, which is suspected of containing Sudan Red — a dye flagged for potential carcinogenicity and allergenic properties. HSA has opened an investigation, will test the product and says it will take regulatory action if safety concerns are confirmed. Consumers who bought it are advised to stop using it as a precaution. Hong Kong Customs issued a warning about the same cream on Jul 24.

stories.headline: Court finds licensed debt collectors broke harassment law pursuing a private debt
stories.summary: In grounds of decision released on Aug 19, Protection from Harassment Court Judge Gregory Gan found employees of a licensed debt collection company breached the Protection from Harassment Act on four occasions — shouting insults and threats at a debtor’s home and visiting her husband’s workplace, then returning to hand his colleagues notices about a debt unrelated to his job. The judge said a licence to collect debts is not “carte blanche” to break the law.

stories.headline: Singaporean, 56, jailed 14 days and fined in Johor for insulting Islam
stories.summary: A Malaysian court sentenced a 56-year-old Singaporean man to 14 days’ jail and a fine of about US$1,733 (S$2,192) for insulting Islam in Johor Bahru. Malaysia treats religious insult as a criminal offence under provisions that carry jail terms, and the case is a reminder to Singaporeans travelling across the Causeway that speech offences there are prosecuted.

stories.headline: P1 priority for parent volunteers, 28 years on: still relevant, or still unfair?
stories.summary: The Straits Times examines the Phase 2B parent-volunteer route into Primary 1, nearly three decades after it began. Supporters say it draws parents into school communities; critics argue it advantages families with the time and flexibility to put in 40 hours of volunteering, and that popular schools are hardest to enter this way. The debate resurfaces each registration cycle without the scheme changing much.

stories.headline: Skilled trades push back on ‘unglam, dirty’ image as the local workforce shrinks
stories.summary: Employers in trades such as electrical work, plumbing and precision engineering say perceptions of the work as dirty and low-status are keeping young Singaporeans away even as their local workforces age out. The piece looks at pay, progression and apprenticeship routes now being used to attract entrants.

stories.headline: ITE student, 18, helps save a grandfather and grandson from a Buangkok flat fire
stories.source: Mothership (Shin Min Daily News), The Straits Times
stories.summary: SCDF was alerted at around 12.25am on Aug 20 to a fire in a second-floor unit at Block 979B Buangkok Crescent, involving the contents of a bedroom. An 18-year-old Institute of Technical Education student living nearby grabbed a fire extinguisher to help fight the flames, helped a grandfather and his eight-year-old grandson out and let them stay in his flat afterwards. The flat owner told Shin Min Daily News his father had been resting when an electrical circuit near the window apparently malfunctioned. One person was taken to Sengkang General Hospital; the cause is under investigation.

stories.headline: Beatty Secondary students track down a wallet’s owner through his NRIC address
stories.summary: A TikTok user posted CCTV footage of three Beatty Secondary School students who found his wallet on a bus and used the address on his NRIC to bring it to his door with the contents intact. When nobody answered, one boy spotted the door camera and held the wallet up to it: “Your wallet right? Eh bro got everything inside. Your money also inside, I never steal.” The clip drew widespread praise.

stories.headline: Customers bring gifts and children to the Roxy Square stallholder shoved over a head pat
stories.summary: Customers have been turning up at the elderly wanton mee stallholder’s Roxy Square shop with gifts and their own children, after he was shoved by a parent for patting a child on the head. One father brought his daughter specifically to encourage the uncle to feel comfortable interacting with young children again. The incident has driven a week of debate in Singapore about how adults greet other people’s children.

stories.headline: Fake Mothership account promotes bogus S$139 Rolex watches
stories.summary: Mothership warned readers about an impersonation account running a new version of a watch-discount scam, this time claiming S$139 deals on Rolexes. The outlet said it offers no watch discounts, that the page appears to have been taken down, and that it is working with the authorities to remove other impersonation accounts. Readers are urged to verify pages and links claiming affiliation before buying anything.

stories.headline: Woman films herself collecting Hungry Ghost Festival fruit offerings, saying produce is expensive here
stories.summary: A woman who said she was from Sichuan and works as a bus driver in Singapore drew backlash after filming herself picking up apples and oranges left as roadside Hungry Ghost Festival offerings, saying on camera: “It’s not easy to work abroad. We have to save every penny. Fruit is so expensive in Singapore!” The video has since been deleted. Shin Min Daily News reported the account; the woman has not been identified publicly.

stories.headline: Singaporean chicken rice stall owner, 46, in alleged Johor road-rage confrontation
stories.summary: A 46-year-old Singaporean chicken rice stall owner was reported to have fought with a Malaysian officer in Johor, with allegations he attacked a 30-year-old woman. The account is based on Malaysian reporting; the allegations have not been tested in court and the outcome of any police action is not yet known.

stories.headline: Taiwan deports Sri Lankan man to Singapore after fake Canadian passport used in transit
stories.summary: Taiwanese authorities deported a Sri Lankan man to Singapore after he was found to have used a fake Canadian passport while transiting through Taiwan. Passengers travelling on forged documents are typically returned to their port of embarkation, which puts the case in the hands of Singapore authorities.

stories.headline: Teen seen with injuries after alleged bullying at Yishun leaves with the group
stories.summary: A passer-by who intervened after seeing a teenage boy with injuries being confronted by a group in Yishun said the boy then left with them anyway. The account comes from the passer-by’s post; no police statement or identification of those involved has been published, and the details have not been independently verified.

stories.headline: Michelin-starred Nouri turns dinner into a play with chef Ivan Brehm acting
stories.summary: Nouri has teamed up with Checkpoint Theatre on a dinner that doubles as a performance, with chef Ivan Brehm taking on an acting role while diners eat. It is one of the more unusual restaurant collaborations to open in Singapore this month.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Russia's escalation is aimed at cities rather than the front line: the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre struck twice on Friday now stands at 16 dead and 130 injured, with nine people still missing after an overnight search. The Iran theatre has gone quiet in the wrong way — no fighting and no talks — with the confrontation resting on Monday's US sanctions announcement and on whether Beijing, which buys most of Iran's shipped oil, goes along with it. Tehran's leverage is a waterway that has effectively closed: four commodity ships transited the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 20, none of them carrying crude or gas. The Israeli-Palestinian theatre is being contested through Interpol filings and settlement bidding rather than battle lines. All three now move faster inside institutions than on the ground, which makes Monday more consequential than anything likely to happen at a front line.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: Russia's air war on cities remains the escalation point, not the front line. A two-wave drone strike on a Kryvyi Rih shopping centre on Aug 21 killed 16 and injured 130, including 23 children, with the second drone arriving about half an hour after the first; rescuers searched the rubble overnight and nine people are still reported missing. At least two more people were killed in further Russian strikes early on Aug 22, and Moscow says it was targeting transport infrastructure and warehouses. Diplomacy is stirring without a track: the French, British and German leaders co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday. The pressure runs both ways — the BBC reports petrol shortages spreading inside Russia after months of Ukrainian strikes on refineries — and the espionage front keeps widening, with German investigators now examining possible Russian links to a weapons cache found in woodland.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.
At least 13 people are killed in a Ukrainian drone strike deep inside Russia, according to Russian officials. The claim has not been independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia is using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine. Moscow and Pyongyang have not confirmed the claim.
Major Russian grain export terminals are hit in a Ukrainian attack on a Black Sea port, extending the campaign against Russian export infrastructure.
Russia dismisses the idea of a Black Sea ceasefire, saying it sees no grounds for 'half-measures' that would give the other side a respite.
NATO jets shoot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace, the latest spillover of the air war into alliance territory.
Russia's defence ministry says its summer campaign has resulted in the capture of 19 settlements in southeastern Ukraine. Kyiv has not confirmed the claim.
Ukraine's General Staff says long-range strikes hit the Progress Rocket Space Centre in Samara, some 900km inside Russia, and a military airfield.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv, which struck blocks of flats and warehouses and damaged a children's hospital and a school. CNA's earlier count was 16. The figures are Ukrainian and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Ukraine State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko tells the BBC that critical infrastructure was 'purposefully attacked' for the first time in several months, disrupting hot water supply in parts of the city.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives.

A senior Russian diplomat says Moscow is ready to consider new ideas on a Ukraine peace settlement but only on its own conditions, repeating that any talks must recognise the 'new realities on the ground'.
Russia holds a rare missile test near the disputed islands north of Japan that Tokyo calls the Northern Territories.

Australia charges a 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen with foreign interference, alleging he joined Ukraine's armed forces to gather information on their military activities for Russia. The allegations have not been tested in court.

Russia's FSB says nine people have been arrested for planned attacks and espionage on behalf of Ukraine, according to Russian state agencies. Kyiv has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.
A Ukrainian man wanted over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage is detained in Croatia, the second arrest in the German-led investigation.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, plans a trip to the United States to raise funding for his projects, The Straits Times reports - a sign his domestic challenge to Zelensky has shifted abroad after the wartime-election protests ended.

The BBC's Steve Rosenberg reports petrol shortages spreading in Russia as the cumulative effect of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure reaches ordinary consumers, though he finds little erosion of public support for the war.
Japan lodges a formal protest over Russia's missile test near the disputed Kuril Islands, held days ahead of an expected Putin visit.

Russian drones strike a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's home city, with a second drone hitting about half an hour after the first. Regional military head Oleksandr Hanzha says 16 people were killed and 130 injured, among them 23 children. Zelensky calls the two-wave attack 'cynical and despicable' and says the second strike targeted emergency workers at the scene; the BBC says it verified footage of the second drone hitting the already burning mall. Russia's military has not commented on the mall.
A separate Russian drone strike in the southern Mykolaiv region kills at least four people, three of them children, and wounds a woman, Ukrainian state media report.
The leaders of France, Britain and Germany announce they will co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday.

Russian state agencies report that nine people have been arrested on suspicion of planning attacks and conducting espionage on Ukraine's behalf. The claim comes from Russian authorities and has not been independently verified.
Russia designates the independent news outlet Mediazona a 'foreign agent'.

German authorities are investigating possible Russian links to a weapons cache discovered in woodland, according to reports cited by the BBC. The investigation is unconfirmed by German officials on the record.

Rescuers work through the night in the wreckage of the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre; Hanzha says the death toll reached 16 after another body was recovered overnight, with nine people reported still missing and 29 in a serious condition. Local officials say at least two more people were killed in further Russian strikes early on Saturday. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted transport infrastructure and warehouses.

theatres.name: US/Israel-Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Neither fighting nor negotiating, with the next move on the calendar rather than the battlefield. Washington will publish its sanctions package on Monday — Bessent has promised 'the toughest sanctions in history' and says the aim is to collapse the government — while Iran's president has signalled he wants to end the war 'in a position of power and dignity' and its armed forces chief promises 'devastating' retaliation. Tehran's leverage is the Strait of Hormuz, where traffic has all but stopped: only four commodity ships transited on Aug 20 and the US says military escorts are moving about 8 million barrels a day, down from more than 20 million before the war. China has rebuffed US requests to help isolate Iran's economy, and NATO members are coordinating escort options outside the alliance framework.

timeline.event: Iran says a deal with Oman on the Strait of Hormuz is in its final stages.
Houthis reportedly kill six people in their first deadly attack since the start of the Iran war.
Yemen's internationally recognised government says the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mocha, killing four civilians. The Houthis have not commented.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the US will step up economic pressure on Iran, as two more ships are reported attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Company says one of its vessels came under attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz the previous day, according to Emirati state media.
Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian', responding to Trump's threat to declare Hormuz US territory.
Yemen's Mocha port suspends commercial and maritime operations after being hit by more than 25 missiles in Houthi attacks over recent days, the port's management says.
Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots, rejecting Tehran's claim that they have been held since Qatari forces downed two Iranian fighter jets.
Iran accuses Qatar of thwarting the investigation into the fate of the three pilots, according to Iranian state-linked media.
Iran's parliament advances a bill further criminalising interviews given to media the state designates as hostile.

Iran's army chief Amir Hatami announces a bounty of about US$30,000 for the killing or capture of US soldiers, saying the plan followed a 'large number of requests' to take part, according to state news agency IRNA.

The US and Iran pass the 60-day deadline set under June's ceasefire memorandum without agreeing a deal on Iran's nuclear programme. Washington has rescinded oil sanctions waivers and reimposed a naval blockade of Iranian ports; Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed.
President Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz, according to a report carried by CNA.
Iran says it now considers the three missing pilots to be prisoners held in Qatar, saying they went missing during an operation against Al Udeid Air Base. Doha denies holding them.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says the group attacked a Saudi military ship and four escort vessels off Yemen's Mocha with missiles. Riyadh has not confirmed the claim.
Drones target the office of the Iraqi Kurdistan region's prime minister; no casualties are reported and no group has claimed responsibility.
Iran says two French embassy employees have been barred from returning to the country.

Iran threatens to 'go on the offensive' in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with the United States fails, and says separately it will escalate if Washington does not honour June's memorandum within weeks. The threats are Tehran's own characterisation.
President Trump says Iran will not agree to the deal he believes is needed, and repeats his threat to strike Oman if it obstructs a Hormuz arrangement.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urges Trump to pursue talks with Iran and offers Ankara's support in facilitating them.
Government bond yields jump and oil extends gains after the US-Iran ceasefire deadline passes without an agreement, with US stocks having fallen in the previous session on the same combination.

Iranian fishermen begin venturing back into waters near the Strait of Hormuz despite fears of renewed fighting, an early sign of civilian activity returning to the waterway even as it stays effectively closed to commercial traffic.

Iran's chief negotiator, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the United States meets Tehran's conditions under the interim deal signed in June. Washington has not publicly responded to the specific terms.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says it received a report that a vessel transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile, causing engine-room damage and one crew casualty. No party has claimed the strike.
The United Arab Emirates says its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran, both of which fell into the sea. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the statement as 'baseless'.

President Donald Trump says talks with Iran are neither taking place nor scheduled and asserts the Strait of Hormuz is open. Iran says the waterway will stay closed until Washington meets the terms of June's interim deal.
Trump posts a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as US territory, days after Iran's deputy foreign minister said the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian'.
France says it will expel two Iranian diplomats in the coming days over a July incident involving two staff of the French embassy in Tehran.
The US Justice Department unseals charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute over hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies.

The United Arab Emirates halts all trade and financial dealings with Iran, saying its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory and that Tehran has repeatedly targeted its tankers. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the missile allegation as baseless.
Iran warns Gulf countries against assisting the United States militarily, after the UAE's decision to cut trade ties.

The Straits Times reports that the UAE's financial embargo puts the long-standing Abu Dhabi-Tehran rivalry back in the spotlight, with the UAE having been one of Iran's largest trade and re-export partners.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slows further as uncertainty over the waterway's status persists.

The US Justice Department's charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute are reported in full, covering hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies. The defendants are not in US custody.
Iran says its ambassador has met four Iranian nationals detained in Kuwait. Kuwaiti authorities have not commented publicly.
An Iranian academic detained in the United States over an alleged link to the 1979 hostage crisis writes about conditions in US detention, in an account published by the BBC.

President Donald Trump says on Truth Social that the United States is launching 'the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country' against Iran, saying Tehran failed to take the chance to make a deal. No sanctions list has been published.

Trump warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Iran 'any type of lifeline' will face 'tremendous economic consequences'. The administration has not named which states it means.

The US warns that Siemens programmable logic controllers can be exploited, amid concern that Iranian-linked actors are breaching water treatment plants. CISA has issued advisories; no confirmed compromise of a US utility has been announced.

Analysts tell Al Jazeera that maintenance problems aboard the carrier USS Abraham Lincoln illustrate the limits of sustaining US naval presence through a prolonged Iran conflict. The Navy has not commented on the assessment.

Trump says he will impose tougher economic measures on Iran and warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Tehran 'any type of lifeline' will face consequences. No sanctions list or named target country has been published.

Iranian officials publicly deride Trump's threat of 'economic warfare'. Separately, Iran's military says it is prepared to conduct offensive strikes as diplomacy with Washington stalls; the statement is Tehran's and has not been independently corroborated.

The Straits Times reports that Iran's practical control over traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is slipping, while the United States is far from having secured the waterway - leaving both sides short of their stated aims.
The US Justice Department charges 17 Iranian nationals linked to the Mabna Institute over an alleged US$3.4 billion theft of academic and corporate data. The defendants are not in US custody.

US agencies including the NSA, CISA, the FBI, the Department of Energy and the EPA warn that attackers are using AI-generated tooling against Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, with water treatment operators among the concerns.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the coming sanctions will be the toughest in history, will 'squash' Iran's economy and that Washington intends to 'collapse this regime', suggesting the move lessens the need for new major military operations. No details of the measures have been released.
The BBC reports that Iran has for years proved adept at working around punishing sanctions, raising doubts about how much the threatened measures would bite.
The US Treasury issues fresh sanctions on Hezbollah, including re-designating it under a terrorism authority, in a move framed around the group's links to the Iranian government.
A new US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been on station for an extended deployment.
Yemen's Houthis say they targeted a Saudi airport and a Saudi Aramco facility. Saudi authorities have not confirmed any damage and the claim is not independently verified.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war: 'It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity.' It is the clearest signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership that Tehran wants an exit, and follows its foreign ministry accusing Washington of 'economic terrorism'.

The chief of staff of Iran's armed forces, Major-General Ali Abdollahi, says Tehran will answer new US threats with 'crushing, punishing and devastating responses' across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, according to Iranian media. Parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Washington appears to have concluded it cannot prevail militarily.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says details of the threatened sanctions package will be published on Aug 24, after saying the measures will be the toughest in history and are intended to collapse the Iranian government.
China says US 'sanctions and pressure' will not resolve the conflict and urges a political solution, rebuffing Washington's request that Beijing help isolate Iran's economy.
A teenager pleads guilty in London over an arson attack on the offices of the Persian-language broadcaster Iran International.

NATO's supreme allied commander, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, hosted a chiefs-of-defence videoconference on Aug 19 to help interested allies coordinate possible contributions to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. His spokesperson stresses it is not a NATO mission; France and Britain have been assembling a coalition of about a dozen countries to guarantee safe passage, which would ultimately need Iranian acquiescence.

President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war 'while we are in a position of power and dignity' - the clearest exit signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership, delivered as Washington prepares to publish its sanctions package on Aug 24.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the imminent US sanctions package an 'assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty over every independent member state of the United Nations' with 'no foundation in international law'. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to detail the measures at a press conference at 2pm EDT on Monday and is pressing Beijing to cooperate; China, which buys more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil on 2025 Kpler data, has urged diplomacy instead. The two sides are neither exchanging fire nor holding talks.

Ship-tracking data shows only four commodity ships transited the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 20, none of them large crude or LNG carriers, with thousands of seafarers stranded on hundreds of vessels. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the US military helped move a seven-day average of 8 million barrels a day through the strait, against more than 20 million a day before the war.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Contested through courts, sanctions and settlement maps rather than battle lines. Turkey said on Aug 21 it will seek an Interpol red notice for Netanyahu over the Gaza aid flotilla; Israel called it a 'pathetic attempt' at intimidation and Netanyahu called Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'. Britain, Canada and Australia condemned Israel's refusal to open a criminal investigation into the killing of aid workers in Gaza, and five governments demanded it drop plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank — where 30 settler families have already moved back into Kadim, evacuated under the 2005 Disengagement Plan. Palestinian officials say Israeli forces shot dead a teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village.

timeline.event: Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers are killed by an explosion.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel rejects President Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza.
Palestinians are told to leave homes in the West Bank village of Qusra that Israeli settlers had besieged.
Israeli forces block activists attempting to deliver aid to Palestinian families besieged by settlers at Qusra.
US officials say Washington wants Netanyahu to publicly condemn the settler siege at Qusra. Netanyahu has not commented publicly.

Israeli airstrikes on Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani in southern Lebanon kill at least 11 people, Lebanon's health ministry says, in the deadliest day since the June truce. Israel says the strikes targeted Hezbollah.
A Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya holds talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo on a plan for Gaza.
US envoy Jared Kushner meets Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo - a rare direct meeting between a senior US official and the group's leadership - while Israel carries out fresh strikes on Gaza.
The Pope calls for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Kushner meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem to push Trump's Gaza plan, a day after the Cairo meeting. Israel rejected the plan on 9 August and has not said whether its position has changed.
UNIFIL says Israeli flags placed along a road in southern Lebanon violate UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Israel has not responded publicly.

Kushner's round of talks with Israel and Hamas ends without a breakthrough on Trump's Gaza plan. US officials say Netanyahu and Kushner discussed Hamas handing over weapons under the supervision of an American general, with disarmament possibly beginning within 30 days; Hamas has not publicly accepted disarmament.

An Israeli settler walks onto the land of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose West Bank home in Qusra has been besieged by settlers, in a tense face-to-face confrontation. The Israeli authorities have not commented on the incident.

An Israeli airstrike kills at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials say, a day after Jared Kushner's regional trip ended without advancing Trump's plan to end the war. Israel has not commented on the strike.
A US envoy says Washington is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria to avoid clashes as all three operate in Syrian territory.

The United States sanctions ICC president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, extending a campaign that began with the court's warrants against Israeli officials over alleged war crimes in Gaza. The ICC says the measures undermine the rule of law.

Syrian state television reports eight Israeli airstrikes on the disused Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province, saying there were no casualties. Damascus calls the attack an unjustified act of aggression.
US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is deeply concerned by Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and calls them an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Turkey rejects as untenable Israel's claim that it struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase to prevent Turkish forces deploying there. Washington says it is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria.

The Israeli military says it has ordered criminal investigations into the January 2024 killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza City and into the killings of Palestinian paramedics and rescue workers. Israel had previously said its forces were unaware of the vehicle Hind Rajab was in.

The International Criminal Court calls the US sanctions on its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye a 'flagrant attack' on the tribunal's independence. Japan separately calls the designations 'unfortunate'.
The BBC reports that thousands of people remain missing in Gaza, with recovery and identification work far behind the scale of the task and families still searching for answers.
Syria arrests an Assad-era officer who had fled Austria after being convicted there.

An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza police station kills nine Palestinians, medics say; Al Jazeera reports the strike hit the Gaza City police headquarters and killed the head of the women's police. Israel has not published its account of the target.

Sources tell The Straits Times that the Mossad chief and Syria's foreign minister discussed Turkish military deployments before Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase. Neither government has confirmed the meeting.
Lebanon hands a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus after an arrest warrant, the first such transfer since Assad's fall.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her family says it does not trust the Israeli judiciary.
The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite its 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen aid worker in Gaza.

Israel opens bidding for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister says he plans sanctions over settlement expansion.
US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee warns Israeli settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans.
The BBC reports multiple deadly Israeli strikes across Gaza in under 24 hours. Casualty figures are from Gaza health officials and have not been independently verified.

Israel and Turkey step up warnings over Syria after Israel's bombing of the Abu al-Duhur airbase; Syria says no Turkish military build-up is planned there. The Straits Times reports Netanyahu is putting Turkey in Israel's crosshairs as an election approaches.

An Assad-era officer is extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges, the first such extradition since Assad's fall, after Lebanon handed a former Assad-era general to Damascus under an arrest warrant.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada issue a joint statement demanding Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, a day after Israel opened bidding. The UN has said the E1 plan poses an 'existential threat' to a contiguous Palestinian state; Israel rejects the criticism.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decided not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian aid worker in Gaza.

Thirty settler families move into Kadim, outside Jenin in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after a previous Israeli government evacuated it under the 2005 Disengagement Plan; the current government has overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attend the ceremony. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.
ICC president Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warns the measures point towards the 'demise of international rule of law'.

The UK, Canada and Australia issue a joint statement calling 'shameful' Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy that killed seven aid workers. Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, says there was 'no criminal intention' and therefore no criminal responsibility.
Israeli forces shoot dead a Palestinian teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village, according to Palestinian officials. The Israeli military's account has not been reported alongside it.

Turkey says it will seek an Interpol notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over Israel's interception of a Gaza aid flotilla, accusing him of genocide. Netanyahu responds by calling President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'. Neither characterisation has been tested in court.

Israel rejects Turkey's move to seek an Interpol red notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the Gaza aid flotilla case, calling it a 'pathetic attempt' to intimidate its leaders and soldiers. Netanyahu calls President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: The DRC's Ebola epidemic is the one to watch: the UN's coordinator says it is now growing faster and wider than the response, across an area larger than France. A vaccine trial against the Bundibugyo strain has just begun, but a trial is not a rollout — there is still no approved vaccine or treatment for this species. Europe's problems are milder and seasonal, with West Nile virus reaching areas that have never reported it and a festival-linked measles cluster now spanning two countries. For readers here the practical risk stays low; the reason to keep following Congo is that the curve has not turned.

outbreaks.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: PHEIC in force since 17 May 2026; the UN's Ebola coordinator says the epidemic is growing exponentially and outrunning the response
outbreaks.scope_note: Laboratory-confirmed cases and deaths in the DRC only, as reported by the DRC health ministry on 20 Aug from data up to 19 Aug and carried in ECDC's Communicable Disease Threats Report for week 34 (published 21 Aug). Six DRC provinces are affected: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo, Haut-Uele and Bas Uele. The country count covers the three countries that have reported confirmed cases across the outbreak — DRC, Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths; Uganda declared its outbreak over on 28 Jul 2026, with no new case since 21 Jun) and France (1 case) — so the DRC figures shown are not a three-country total. WHO's latest formal Disease Outbreak News (DON615, 14 Aug, data to 12 Aug) puts the cumulative confirmed total at 4,686 cases and 2,186 deaths, of which DRC 4,665 cases and 2,184 deaths, a 46.8 per cent case fatality rate; the newer DRC figures are not yet DON-ratified. UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis said on 21 Aug that deaths now top 2,500, that about 160 health workers have fallen ill and 43 have died, and that there have been more than 260 attacks on health workers in the past six months.

outbreaks.name: Europe — West Nile virus (2026 season)
outbreaks.status: Seasonal transmission expanding; 21 areas affected for the first time this season
outbreaks.scope_note: Locally acquired human infections in the 2026 transmission season. ECDC's week-34 threats report (21 Aug) counts 98 affected areas across 12 countries as at 21 Aug — Italy 46, Greece 16, Romania 14, France 8, North Macedonia 3, Serbia 3, Spain 3, and one each in Albania, Austria, Germany, Kosovo and the Netherlands — of which 21 are affected for the first time this season. ECDC does not publish an EU/EEA-wide case total in the report itself; the Italy 311 and Greece 157 figures are ECDC numbers reported via AFP and The Straits Times on 21 Aug, which counted 99 rather than 98 affected regions. For comparison, 67 regions in nine countries had reported cases by the same point in August 2025. No death toll is published.

outbreaks.name: Sweden & Finland — measles cluster linked to a music festival
outbreaks.status: Contained to festival contacts so far; most cases unvaccinated under-18s
outbreaks.scope_note: Cases identified as at 21 Aug across nine regions in Sweden and one in Finland, all epidemiologically linked to a music festival held in Sweden's Västernorrland Region from 30 July to 1 August, per ECDC's week-34 Communicable Disease Threats Report. The festival drew about 10,000 people, roughly 10 per cent from outside Sweden, mainly Norway. Most cases are unvaccinated children and adolescents under 18. Finland reported its case on 21 Aug in Åland, in a person who had travelled on two ferries between Åland and Sweden after exposure. No deaths reported.

outbreaks.name: Europe — Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 multi-country cluster
outbreaks.status: Ongoing, with new cases still being reported
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed cases reported between May 2025 and August 2026 across seven European countries, per ECDC's week-34 Communicable Disease Threats Report (21 Aug), with a notable increase in notifications since May 2026 and new cases at the start of August 2026. Additional cases whose isolates cluster with the outbreak strain have been confirmed in the United Kingdom. ECDC does not publish a death toll for this cluster.

stories.headline: UN says Congo's Ebola outbreak is spreading exponentially across an area larger than France
stories.summary: Senior UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis said on Aug 21, speaking from Bunia, that more than 2,500 people have now died and that the epidemic is 'growing faster and wider than the Ebola response' across an area bigger than France.
