He said existing funds run out within weeks, that about 160 health workers have fallen ill and 43 have died, and that there have been more than 260 attacks on health workers in six months, with ambulances burned and clinics attacked. The DRC's 17th Ebola epidemic became the country's largest by case count in late July; the Bundibugyo species has no approved vaccine or treatment.

stories.headline: DR Congo begins an Ebola vaccine trial against the Bundibugyo strain
stories.summary: A vaccine trial is starting in the DRC against the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, for which no vaccine or specific treatment is approved — the existing licensed Ebola vaccines target the Zaire species. The launch came alongside a warning about how fast infections are now spreading. A trial is not a rollout: it will take time to produce usable evidence, so case-finding, safe burials and contact tracing remain the only tools on the ground.

stories.headline: West Nile virus reported in 12 European countries as ECDC urges stronger mosquito control
stories.summary: ECDC said on Aug 21 that 12 European countries have reported locally acquired West Nile cases this season, with Italy (311) and Greece (157) the highest, and called for stronger mosquito control. The agency counted 98 affected areas in its week-34 threats report — AFP and The Straits Times reported 99 regions — against 67 regions in nine countries by the same point in 2025. Most infections are mild or symptom-free, but the virus can cause encephalitis or meningitis, and there is no vaccine or specific treatment for humans.

stories.headline: ECDC's week-34 report flags a festival-linked measles cluster in Sweden and Finland
stories.summary: As at Aug 21, 27 measles cases have been identified across nine Swedish regions and one in Finland, all linked to a music festival held in Västernorrland from Jul 30 to Aug 1 that drew about 10,000 people. Most cases are unvaccinated children and adolescents. Finland's case, reported on Aug 21 in Åland, had travelled on two ferries between Åland and Sweden after exposure. Swedish authorities are working with regional communicable disease units to limit further spread.

stories.headline: ECDC tracks an ongoing seven-country Salmonella Enteritidis cluster with 341 cases
stories.summary: ECDC's week-34 threats report records 341 confirmed Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 cases across seven European countries between May 2025 and August 2026, with notifications rising notably since May 2026 and new cases at the start of this month. Cases whose isolates match the outbreak strain have also been confirmed in the UK. A vehicle for the cluster has not been published.

stories.headline: ECDC's week-34 threats report also tracks swine flu, avian influenza, dengue, chikungunya and Crimean-Congo fever
stories.summary: Alongside Ebola and West Nile, ECDC's Aug 21 report logs one human case of swine influenza A(H1N2)v in Michigan, reported on Aug 14 in a swine exhibitor at an agricultural fair, and one human case of avian influenza A(H9N2) in Yunnan, China, in a child under five who recovered and was discharged. It also carries the weekly seasonal surveillance for dengue, chikungunya and Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, and a cluster of Dermatophilus congolensis infection in the EU/EEA. None currently changes the risk picture for travellers from Singapore.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch Microsoft Entra ID first: CVE-2026-69836 is a CVSS 10.0 deserialisation flaw that Microsoft says is already being exploited, and it sits at the identity layer for Microsoft 365 and Azure. Four more exploited flaws landed on CISA's catalog this week, the fastest of them a GitLab bug attackers reached within days of the advisory. The urgent-but-not-yet-exploited tier is unusually crowded, led by five CVSS 10.0 issues in Cisco Crosswork and Secure Workload and an unauthenticated file upload in Elementor Pro that puts a very large number of WordPress sites in range. Two supply-chain incidents deserve separate handling: poisoned Rust crates with 245 million downloads that run at build time, and 14 trojanised npm packages dropping a Linux backdoor. If you do only two things this weekend, fix Entra ID and rebuild anything that compiled Rust dependencies in the last few days.

stories.headline: 14 trojanised npm packages drop a RedC2 4.0 Linux backdoor with AI-assisted command and control
stories.summary: Fourteen malicious npm packages were found installing a Linux backdoor identified as RedC2 4.0, whose operators use AI assistance in the command-and-control workflow. Anyone who pulled the affected packages should treat build hosts as compromised, rotate credentials reachable from them and pin dependencies to known-good versions.

stories.headline: Microsoft Defender’s own boot-time driver can be turned against security software
stories.source: The Hacker News, Check Point Research
stories.summary: Researchers showed that a signed Microsoft Defender driver that runs early in the boot sequence can be manipulated to delete security software files before those products start, giving an attacker with sufficient local privileges a way to disarm defences using a trusted Microsoft component. Watch for unexpected deletions of security-product files at boot and confirm tamper protection is enabled.

stories.headline: Android car malware spreads through built-in vehicle updaters for ad fraud and proxy botnets
stories.summary: Malware targeting Android-based in-vehicle infotainment systems is being distributed through the units’ own built-in update mechanisms, enrolling cars into ad-fraud and residential-proxy operations. Using the manufacturer’s update channel makes this a supply-chain problem rather than a user-installed-app problem, and the affected units are rarely covered by conventional endpoint tooling.

stories.headline: Hundreds of leaked AWS keys found giving full control over corporate accounts
stories.summary: Researchers found hundreds of exposed AWS access keys that granted full administrative control over corporate accounts, harvested from public code, container images and other artefacts. Rotate long-lived keys, move to short-lived credentials or roles, and turn on automated secret scanning across repositories and build pipelines.

stories.headline: CISA orders federal agencies to patch two actively exploited TrueConf Server flaws
stories.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-72530 (CVSS 9.5, code injection) and CVE-2026-72529 (CVSS 9.3, missing authentication) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Aug 20 and issued a patch directive to federal agencies. NVD records both as reachable by an unauthenticated remote attacker over port 4307/TCP against TrueConf Server 5.3.x to 5.3.9, 5.4.x to 5.4.9, 5.5.x to 5.5.5 and earlier. Restrict access to port 4307 and update immediately.

stories.headline: Microsoft warns of a maximum-severity Entra ID flaw exploited in attacks
stories.summary: NVD describes CVE-2026-69836 as deserialization of untrusted data in Microsoft Entra ID that lets an unauthorized attacker execute code over a network, scored CVSS 10.0 and published on Aug 20. Microsoft says it has been exploited in attacks. Because Entra ID is the identity layer for Microsoft 365 and Azure, treat this as the highest-priority item this cycle: apply Microsoft’s guidance, then review sign-in and privileged-role changes for anomalies.

stories.headline: Cisco patches nine Crosswork and Secure Workload flaws, five scoring CVSS 10.0
stories.source: The Hacker News, Cisco advisory, NVD
stories.summary: Cisco disclosed nine vulnerabilities in Crosswork and Secure Workload following an internal security review, five of them rated CVSS 10.0. NVD confirms CVE-2026-20030 at 10.0, published Aug 19. There is no report of exploitation yet, but these are network-management and workload-security platforms with broad reach inside an estate, so patch on the fast track rather than the normal cycle.

stories.headline: Hackers abuse FTP server banners to deliver new Windows malware
stories.summary: A campaign is hiding payload stages inside FTP server greeting banners, a channel that most inspection tooling treats as harmless metadata. The technique lets the delivery traffic look like ordinary protocol chatter; defenders should make sure outbound FTP is logged and inspected rather than assumed benign.

stories.headline: SickKids data breach exposes employee and job applicant information
stories.summary: Toronto’s Hospital for Sick Children disclosed a breach exposing employee and job applicant data. Patient care systems were not reported as affected. Applicant databases are a recurring soft target because they hold identity documents but often sit outside the controls applied to clinical systems.

stories.headline: GitLab CVE-2026-19478 comes under active exploitation days after disclosure
stories.summary: Attackers began exploiting CVE-2026-19478 within days of GitLab’s advisory. NVD scores it 9.4 and lists GitLab CE/EE from 18.2 before 18.11.11, 19.0 before 19.0.8, 19.1 before 19.1.6 and 19.2 before 19.2.4 as affected. Self-managed GitLab instances are a direct route to source code and CI secrets — patch, then audit tokens and runner credentials.

stories.headline: Rust supply chain attack plants build-time malware in crates with 245 million downloads
stories.summary: Attackers poisoned widely used Rust crates — BleepingComputer names arrayref among them — to run infostealer code at build time rather than at runtime, across packages with a combined 245 million downloads. Build-time execution means a developer or CI machine is compromised the moment it compiles, before any binary ships. Audit Cargo.lock, rebuild from clean hosts and rotate anything a build agent could read.

stories.headline: Suspected Russian hackers abuse Google OAuth and WhatsApp device linking to hijack accounts
stories.summary: A campaign attributed to suspected Russian operators chains Google OAuth consent flows with WhatsApp’s linked-device feature to take over accounts without stealing a password. Because both steps use legitimate functionality, the takeover survives password resets — users should check linked devices and connected apps, not just change credentials.

stories.headline: AI-generated exploit scripts target Siemens S7 PLCs in US critical infrastructure
stories.summary: Researchers observed exploit scripts, apparently generated with AI assistance, aimed at Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers in US critical infrastructure. The scripts lower the skill floor for attacking industrial controllers that were never designed to be internet-reachable. Operators should confirm S7 devices are not exposed and that engineering workstations are segmented from IT networks.

stories.headline: Cryptographic context injection attack could let web pages steal Grok chat data
stories.summary: A new attack class lets an ordinary web page manipulate cryptographic context to read a user’s Grok conversation data. It is the latest in a run of browser-adjacent AI assistant flaws where the trust boundary between a page and the assistant is thinner than users assume — a reason to be cautious about what is pasted into browser-integrated assistants.

stories.headline: isolated-vm flaw lets sandboxed JavaScript escape to the host
stories.summary: A flaw in the isolated-vm Node.js library allows code running inside what is meant to be a sandboxed isolate to reach the host process, opening a path to remote code execution. Anyone using isolated-vm to run untrusted or user-supplied JavaScript — a common pattern in plugin and serverless-style platforms — should update and re-examine what the host process can access.

stories.headline: Critical Elementor Pro bug lets unauthenticated attackers upload PHP and run code
stories.summary: NVD records CVE-2026-32475 as an unrestricted file upload in Elementor Pro affecting versions up to and including 4.2.1, scored 9.0 and published Aug 19. It allows an unauthenticated attacker to upload a PHP file and execute code on the site. Elementor Pro is on a very large number of WordPress sites, which historically means mass scanning follows quickly — update now and check the uploads directory for stray PHP files.

stories.headline: Critical NetScaler flaw bypasses authentication on Gateway and AAA servers
stories.summary: NVD scores CVE-2026-19490 at 9.3 and lists NetScaler ADC 14.1 through 73.32 and 13.1 through 63.21, and Gateway on the same ranges, as affected when configured as a Gateway or AAA virtual server. Citrix is urging admins to patch as soon as possible. NetScaler appliances sit at the network edge and have been repeatedly targeted after disclosure, so treat the window between advisory and exploitation as short.

stories.headline: Attackers exploit a Zimbra SNMP flaw for unauthenticated remote code execution
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD
stories.summary: CVE-2026-73570 is an OS command injection in Zimbra Collaboration before 10.1.20 that is only reachable when the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled. NVD scores it 8.9; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Aug 21. Upgrade to 10.1.20 or, if you cannot, remove the zimbra-snmp package or disable SNMP notifications.

stories.headline: ‘Zombie Card’ attack can revive expired Visa cards for contactless payments
stories.summary: Researchers demonstrated a technique that makes expired Visa cards usable again for contactless payments, by exploiting how expiry is validated in the tap flow. It matters for anyone who assumes a cancelled or lapsed card is inert — check statements on old cards rather than treating expiry as an automatic stop.

stories.headline: CDN Tsunami attack abuses HTTP/3 translation for up to 350x DoS amplification
stories.summary: Researchers showed that the way some CDNs translate between HTTP/3 and older protocol versions can be abused to amplify traffic by up to 350 times, turning the delivery network itself into the amplifier. Operators should check whether their CDN configuration permits the translation pattern involved and apply the vendor guidance as it appears.

stories.headline: NASA AIT-GUI flaws could let unauthenticated attackers issue spacecraft commands
stories.summary: Flaws in NASA’s open-source AIT-GUI ground-software toolkit could allow an unauthenticated attacker to issue spacecraft commands. AIT is used well beyond NASA by smaller satellite and research programmes, so the relevant question for any operator is whether an AIT deployment is reachable from an untrusted network at all.

stories.headline: CISA warns of hackers exploiting a critical MLflow vulnerability
stories.summary: CVE-2026-64849 is a server-side request forgery in MLflow before 3.15.0, reachable through an unauthenticated webhooks endpoint; NVD scores it 9.3. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Aug 19, and attackers have used it to steal cloud credentials and secrets. MLflow servers often run inside environments with generous cloud roles attached — patch to 3.15.0 and rotate any credentials the instance could reach.

stories.headline: Cloudflare Workers Spectre attack leaks a JWT from a co-located worker
stories.summary: Researchers used a Spectre-style side channel to read a JSON web token belonging to a different tenant’s worker sharing the same process, at roughly 12 bits per second. The rate is slow, but it re-opens the question of isolation between tenants in shared serverless runtimes — relevant to anyone relying on process co-location for separation rather than hard isolation.

stories.headline: SilkParasite espionage campaign targets Central Asian governments with five new RATs
stories.summary: A campaign tracked as SilkParasite has been targeting government bodies across Central Asia with five previously undocumented remote access trojans. The number of distinct new tools points to a resourced operator building for long-term access rather than a smash-and-grab, and gives defenders in the region concrete families to hunt for.

stories.headline: More than 14,500 Dahua devices compromised via credential attacks and auth bypasses
stories.summary: Attackers compromised more than 14,500 Dahua surveillance devices using credential attacks, authentication bypasses and the vendor’s peer-to-peer connectivity feature. The P2P path is the awkward part: it is designed to work through NAT, so a camera can be reachable even when an operator believes it is behind a firewall. Change default credentials, patch firmware and disable P2P where it is not needed.

stories.headline: Critical macOS, SharePoint, vCenter and Microsoft IKE flaws under active exploitation
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD
stories.summary: CISA added four exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Aug 18: CVE-2026-65400 in Apple macOS (an authentication issue fixed in Sequoia 15.7.9, Sonoma 14.8.9 and Tahoe 26.6.1, NVD 9.8), CVE-2026-55040 weak authentication in Microsoft SharePoint, CVE-2026-59310 path traversal in Broadcom VMware vCenter, and CVE-2026-33824 a double-free in Microsoft’s IKE service extensions. All four are in widely deployed enterprise software and all four are being exploited now.
